newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says not to buy rest of Mendes.
newsitem.headline: ING says not to buy rest of Mendes.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Tuesday it did not intend to buy the remaining stake of about seven percent in bank Mendes Gans that it does not already own.
"We are not going to do so because the price is not realistic," executive board chairman Aad Jacobs told ING's annual shareholder meeting.
ING earlier on Tuesday reached agreement to buy the 34.2 percent stake in Mendes from Philips. This will lift ING's interest in Mendes to 93.3 percent.
Jacobs said ING did not pay the current share price for the increased stake. On Tuesday after the deal, Mendes Gans shares were trading at 19,500 guilders, up 205 guilders on the day.
An ING spokesman told Reuters the price paid would not be revealed as it was a private matter between ING and Philips.
Mendes Gans operates integrated cash management systems and information systems and is active in asset management, custody and portfolio management systems, ING said in a statement.
